name: Vāci yoga (the Siddhar breath-yoga)
method_summary: Summary only: the Siddhars' mastery of the breath, imaged as binding the 'horse of twelve feet' (TM 722), placing the prāṇa in vāci after initiation (Caṭṭaimuṉi 4), so that the body becomes firm and long-lived and the breath is turned inward towards the root and crown. No counts, ratios or retention times are recorded.

equivalents.note: vāci includes breath-restraint but is framed as body-perfection and inner turning

signs_of_progress: the texts claim an undecaying body and long life (TM 722)

warnings.text: Kāya-citti and vāci are joined to initiation (tīṭcai) and the guru; 'the Siddhars' worship' requires initiation.
For the true knower who has seen the true thing, kaṟpam and yoga are needless (the means are not the goal).

notes: Restricted as a retention-based practice; the texts' claims are recorded as claims.

name: Kāya kaṟpam (rejuvenation of the body)
method_summary: Summary only: regimens held to make the body firm, remove the humours at their times, reverse grey hair and wrinkles (TM 727) and prolong life for yoga — herbal kaṟpam, breath and yogic kaṟpam, and mineral-metal kaṟpam. No preparations, doses or durations are recorded; the mineral and mercurial forms are restricted.

equivalents.note: Āyurvedic rejuvenation; the Siddha form includes yogic and breath means

signs_of_progress: grey hair and wrinkles perish; the body becomes lustrous 'like collyrium' (TM 727) — the text's claim

warnings.text: Mineral and metal medicines are poison unless purified and prepared exactly as taught by a guru, and must be taken under strict regimen (pattiyam).
For the true knower who has seen the true thing, kaṟpam and yoga are needless (the means are not the goal).
All the powers — even transmuting metals and entering another's body — are easier than stilling the mind; the powers are not the goal.

name: Herbal kaṟpam (kaṟpa mūlikai)
method_summary: Summary only: the use of particular herbs regarded as rejuvenating (the tradition names, among others, kaṭukkāy (chebulic myrobalan), nellikkāy (emblic), karicālai (false daisy) and vallārai), taken as a long regimen under a physician's direction. No doses or preparations recorded.

warnings.text: Kaṟpam is taken only after purging and under the prescribed regimen; the physician decides.

notes: Herb names recalled at moderate confidence; the full list of kaṟpa herbs is not reconstructed.

name: Siddhar alchemy (iracavātam: mercury, pāṣāṇam, muppu)
method_summary: Summary only: the Siddhar art of 'binding' mercury, purifying and calcining poisonous minerals and using the secret salt (muppu), both to transmute metals and to make the body deathless; Bogar's Palani image of nine pāṣāṇams is its emblem. No substances, quantities or processes are recorded.

warnings.text: The knowledge is veiled in code language and given only to a proven disciple; unpurified mercury and pāṣāṇam are deadly poison.
All the powers — even transmuting metals and entering another's body — are easier than stilling the mind; the powers are not the goal.
For the true knower who has seen the true thing, kaṟpam and yoga are needless (the means are not the goal).

name: Amuri tāraṇai (TM 3rd tantra)
method_summary: Summary only: a section of the Tirumantiram's third tantra, read in the Siddha tradition as the use of a bodily 'nectar' (amuri) for rejuvenation. Nothing further recorded.
notes: Restricted (bodily-substance practice). Section title checked in the local TM e-text; interpretation low.

name: Khecarī (TM kēcari yōkam)
method_summary: Summary only: the Tirumantiram's third tantra has a section on kēcari yōkam, revered by the Siddhars; recorded as a restricted summary without method.
notes: U22 contribution to the shared entry; section title checked in the local TM e-text.

name: Siddhar rites against enemies
method_summary: Summary only: some Siddhar worship-manuals (Rāmatēvar's Pūjāviti 5–7) include rites for striking down an enemy. No procedure recorded.

warnings.text: Is one to curse? Do no cruel deeds.

name: Entering living samādhi (cīva camāti)
method_summary: Summary only: the tradition's account that a Siddhar, at the end, enters samādhi and is enclosed alive in a shrine, remaining present there. Recorded as the tradition's account; no instructions.
notes: Restricted (ends in death); belief recorded, no procedure.

name: Worship of Vālai / Maṉōṉmaṇi at the root and on the Meru
method_summary: The Siddhars' Śākta worship: the goddess Vālai (Bālā), mother Maṉōṉmaṇi, is worshipped at the root centre with her three syllables and on the Meru of forty-three triangles (the Śrīcakra), with the syllables of Tripurā, Bhuvanā and Yāmaḷā, after the five initiations (Rāmatēvar; Caṭṭaimuṉi). Mantras and procedure not recorded.

equivalents.note: the Meru of 43 triangles is the Śrīcakra

warnings.text: Worship done 'by the deluded' becomes waste; the Meru needs initiation, 'a small child cannot touch it'.

name: Tirumūlar's eightfold yoga
method_summary: The eight limbs (iyamam, niyamam, ātaṉam, pirāṇāyāmam, pirattiyākāram, tāraṇai, tiyāṉam, camāti — TM 552), commended by the Siddhar poets (Kaṭuveḷi 31).

name: Gaze at the middle of the brows
method_summary: Passing beyond the supports, the yogin gazes at the middle of eyes, nose and forehead and on the guru as a flame of grace (Tirumūla ñāṉam 5); Pattirakiriyār longs to see the light of bliss straight at the forehead (227).

name: Being still (cummā iruttal)
method_summary: The silent guru's instruction 'be still': resting without the mind's movement, which Tāyumāṉavar holds harder and higher than every power.

warnings.text: All the powers — even transmuting metals and entering another's body — are easier than stilling the mind; the powers are not the goal.

name: Sleeping without sleeping (Śiva-yoga sleep)
method_summary: Remaining in the unceasing 'sleep of Śiva-yoga', senses withdrawn and awareness awake (Pattirakiriyār 1–2; Kuṭampai 6).

equivalents.note: sleep-like state kept aware; different texts and methods

name: Silence (mauṉam)
method_summary: Taking the form of a mute and drawing in the senses like a tortoise (Pattirakiriyār 19); the silent guru's teaching.

name: Self-inquiry ('who am I?')
method_summary: Pattirakiriyār longs to realize 'who am I, who are you, who is the Supreme' (225) and to know all he sees as 'I am He' (219).

name: Inner worship without outer offerings
method_summary: Worship in which the heart is the temple and no ablution or flower is offered: 'without bath-offering or flowers, the heart stood empty' (Aḻukaṇṇi 37); the temple and tank are in the mind (Sivavākkiyar).

name: Repetition of the five letters
method_summary: Chanting the five letters to the Dancer at Tillai yields birthless release (Paṭṭiṉattār).

name: Non-killing (kollāmai)
method_summary: Not killing, tormenting or eating living beings, regarding them as one's own life (Pattirakiriyār 14); do not throw stones at birds or kill a frightened life (Kaṭuveḷi 25, 29).

name: Refusing flesh (pulāl maṟuttal)
method_summary: Paṭṭiṉattār's warning to those who kill for the belly (Tiruvēkampamālai 33).

name: Total renunciation (tuṟavu)
method_summary: Giving up house, wealth, kin and body-pride at a stroke, as Paṭṭiṉattār did on reading 'even an eyeless needle will not come'; the renouncer-in-mind is highest (Tiruvēkampamālai 1); seeing kin as false (Pattirakiriyār 13).

name: Dispassion
method_summary: Living without attachment to the world, knowing the body a bubble (Kaṭuveḷi 3), like a lotus leaf on water (Pattirakiriyār 54).

name: Service of the devotees
method_summary: Tāyumāṉavar asks to be made a servant for the service of devotees, from which the state of bliss comes of itself.

name: Seeking and worshipping the guru
method_summary: Seeking the master (āriyaṉ) and bowing at his feet (Pattirakiriyār 26); gazing daily on the guru as the flame of grace and seeing the Lord as the guru (Tirumūla ñāṉam 5–6).

name: Day-wise breath (vāra caram)
method_summary: The Tirumantiram's third tantra has sections on the breath flowing through the left or right nostril by weekday (vāra caram, vāra cūlam), read by the Siddhas; summary only.

equivalents.note: svara lore of the nostril breath

notes: Section titles checked in the local TM e-text; contents not summarized.

name: Siddha daily regimen (nōy aṇukā viti)
method_summary: Rules by which disease does not approach: eat only after the previous meal is digested and in measure (Kuṟaḷ 942, 946); regular oil-baths, moderate sleep, restraint and seasonal adjustment as taught in the verses ascribed to Tēraiyar.
notes: Tēraiyar's specific rules recalled only in outline (low).

name: Tokkaṇam (Siddha therapeutic massage)
method_summary: Therapeutic massage and manipulation, one of the external treatments of Siddha medicine, practised in several named kinds. No techniques recorded.
